local.h: Forsyth voters flagged as dead were found alive
local.b: ProPublica found that a Forsyth County election board member challenged dozens of ballots using a data tool built by an election denier network, and some voters it called dead are alive.
local.title: A Tool Built by Election Deniers Said These Voters Were Dead. We Found Them Alive.

local.h: Bidding closes on Georgia warehouses ICE bought
local.b: Offers are due Thursday on ICE-purchased warehouses, including a $128 million site in Social Circle meant to hold up to 10,000 people. A GAO report found ICE wasted taxpayer money expanding detention.
local.title: Bidding deadline ends for Georgia warehouses ditched by ICE

local.h: Georgia's Latino voters swing toward Democrats
local.b: About 198,000 Latinos voted in Georgia's midterms, up 78% from 2022, and polling showed 72% backed Sen. Jon Ossoff. Advocates warn it's a misalignment, not a realignment, and both parties must earn their votes.
local.title: Georgia’s Latinos shift toward Democratic candidates, for now

local.h: Healey plans pilot to bring military medics into hospitals
local.b: The administration unveiled a pilot letting a limited number of veteran medics work at certain hospitals without additional training, aiming to ease staff shortages.

local.h: Paul George scores 36 as Celtics rout 76ers
local.b: George hit six 3-pointers in his return to Philadelphia and Jayson Tatum added 21 as Boston won 123-101 for its ninth win in 10 games, outplaying former teammate Jaylen Brown.

goodnews.h: Cambridge home baker's cookies sell out in minutes
goodnews.b: Hope Truwit's Butter & Hope baked goods took off after a local influencer shared them, with one customer driving 40 minutes for a cookie.

local.h: CPS students could lose Google search over AI rules
local.b: Districts that bar popular AI tools in classrooms, like Chicago Public Schools, will lose access to Google search next year. CPS says it has guidelines to help students and teachers use AI safely.

local.h: Lawmakers probe deadly fires at Joliet prison
local.b: State legislators held a hearing after a Marshall Project, WBEZ and Sun-Times investigation found 70 fires at the Joliet Treatment Center, where men in mental health care set fires in despair over conditions. Two died.

local.h: Police sergeant dies after being found unresponsive at station
local.b: Sgt. Timothy Martin, 49, was found unresponsive on duty at the Albany Park District station and later pronounced dead. The medical examiner hasn't ruled on a cause.

local.h: Amazon drone delivery center coming to Markham
local.b: Amazon says drone deliveries will start this fall from a new center at 2201 W. 159th St. in Markham, part of a suburban expansion. The drones carry packages up to five pounds.

goodnews.h: Illinois Holocaust Museum reopens after renovation
goodnews.b: The Skokie museum reopens Wednesday after 15 months and more than $10 million in upgrades, including a reflection gallery, new artifacts and a 240-seat auditorium.

local.h: Lakewood officer killed on RTD bus remembered at funeral
local.b: Agent Nicholas Graham was killed in a shootout aboard an RTD bus last week.
local.title: Lakewood Police agent killed in bus shooting remembered at public funeral service

local.h: Mountain View keeps its strong-mayor system
local.b: After months of political drama, a measure to change the town's political structure failed a second time.
local.title: After months of political drama, Mountain View decides to keep things the same

local.h: Denver weighs renters' unions and tougher landlord rules
local.b: Some City Council members are proposing to let renters unionize and strengthen regulations beyond the city's current power to fine landlords for violations.
local.title: Denver considers allowing renters’ unions and cracking down on landlords

local.h: Citywide upzoning back on the table in Denver
local.b: Denver's "Unlocking Housing Choices" proposal has been expanded once more, reviving a citywide upzoning push.
local.title: A citywide upzoning is back on the menu in Denver

goodnews.h: Couples tie the knot with Elvis on Colfax
goodnews.b: More than a dozen couples were married by an Elvis impersonator at the Bluebird Theater.
goodnews.title: Who needs the Elvis chapel in Vegas when we’ve got Colfax?

local.h: State gives $1 million to study Pacific Surfliner fixes
local.b: The rail agency will update a reliability study, including how the 2028 Olympics could affect service on the erosion-plagued line.
local.title: Agency overseeing Amtrak Pacific Surfliner to get $1 million from state to study improvements

local.h: Raman promises to halve street homelessness before Olympics
local.b: Mayor-elect Nithya Raman says her plan will cut street homelessness by 50% in time for the 2028 Games and end long-term encampments by the end of her first term.
local.title: Nithya Raman’s big Olympics promise: Reduce street homelessness by 50%

local.h: Doctors' group backs ban on stone linked to deadly lung disease
local.b: The American Medical Association now opposes making, selling and installing high-silica engineered stone countertops, linked to silicosis killing stoneworkers in California.
local.title: Largest US doctors’ group supports banning countertop material linked to deadly lung disease

local.h: Driver arrested in deadly Metro station crash
local.b: Police arrested the 61-year-old minivan driver whose rush-hour crash outside a Los Angeles Metro station killed three, on suspicion of DUI and three counts of murder.

goodnews.h: Original Pantry Cafe reopens with a new mission
goodnews.b: The century-old downtown diner, closed since March 2025, reopens Nov. 19 run by nonprofit Hope the Mission, with all profits going to shelters for unhoused Angelenos and longtime staff returning under a union contract.
goodnews.title: The Original Pantry Cafe returns with a new menu and mission

local.h: Feds charge gang members in 2022 killing of 12-year-old
local.b: Prosecutors say members of a Brooklyn gang fired into the wrong car in East Flatbush, killing a 12-year-old boy, after mistaking it for a rival's.
local.title: Feds say gang members killed 12-year-old in East Flatbush drive-by, targeting a rival

local.h: Developer next to Flatbush collapse had flouted city orders
local.b: Buildings department records show the owner of the lot being excavated beside the collapsed building kept demolishing after a stop work order earlier this year and was penalized again.
local.title: Developer at Brooklyn collapse site had record of flouting orders from city agency

local.h: Bill would make delivery apps pay for e-bike fixes
local.b: A City Council bill from Councilmember Harvey Epstein would require food delivery companies to fund fixes for crowded e-bike parking, like the East Village block where hundreds of bikes line the curb.
local.title: NYC bill would require food delivery firms to fund fixes to the e-bike 'crisis'

local.h: New Yorkers line up to become casino dealers
local.b: Big Deal Casino Academy in NoMad, the city's only Education Department-licensed dealer school, is scaling up as New York City's first full-scale casino, in Jamaica, finally arrives.
local.title: A good bet: New Yorkers are lining up to become casino dealers

local.h: Greenpoint street redesign previews 'low-traffic' plan
local.b: New diverters on Driggs Avenue force drivers to turn near McGolrick Park, a model city lawmakers want citywide. A ballot measure passed last week could speed such redesigns.
local.title: North Brooklyn street redesign paves the way for NYC's 'low-traffic neighborhood' plan

local.h: Flatbush building collapse death toll rises to eight
local.b: City officials said Thursday the collapse of a three-story apartment building in Flatbush has killed eight people and injured at least 25, including at least seven children, as crews kept searching the rubble.
local.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills 6 adults, 2 children and rescue work still underway, mayor says

local.h: East Side's Cinema 123 closes after 60 years
local.b: The Angelika theater near the Queensboro Bridge screened its last film after its building sold to Roger Equities for $41 million, weeks after the Kips Bay AMC announced it will close.
local.title: Manhattan’s East Side loses another movie theater to development

local.h: Teen arrested in killing of Bronx boy walking to school
local.b: Police arrested a 17-year-old in the Oct. 29 shooting death of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong near Crotona Park. The motive is not yet clear.
local.title: Teen arrested for fatal shooting of 15-year-old Bronx boy walking to school, NYPD says

local.h: Sanitation supervisors rack up speed camera tickets
local.b: Gothamist found 763 sanitation department cars assigned to supervisors and other staff have collected at least 2,375 speed camera tickets since 2023. Advocates want faster rollout of speed limiters, which Mayor Mamdani supports.
local.title: NYC sanitation supervisors keep speeding on the job, data shows

local.h: Chelsea NYCHA redevelopment splits Mamdani's allies
local.b: Tenant activists at Fulton and Elliott-Chelsea Houses have joined DSA to fight the $1.2 billion plan to replace about 2,000 public housing units with mixed-income development, calling it privatization. Mamdani says a teardown is cheaper than repairs.
local.title: Mamdani’s redevelopment plan for NYCHA complex in Chelsea spills into DSA

goodnews.h: Housing slashed homeless New Yorkers' ER costs, study finds
goodnews.b: A small study found health care costs fell sharply for homeless patients after NYC Health and Hospitals helped house them, while their spending on preventive care rose.
goodnews.title: Homeless New Yorkers’ healthcare costs plummeted after getting housed, study finds

goodnews.h: Lost Georgia O'Keeffe painting found in East Village closet
goodnews.b: A niece helping her aunt settle her affairs found O'Keeffe's landscape "Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I" in a wooden box behind coats. Christie's specialists called the find exceptional.
goodnews.title: Long-lost Georgia O’Keeffe painting found in East Village closet

local.h: France bars prominent Israeli settler leader
local.b: Yossi Dagan was turned back at a Paris airport over his role in West Bank settlement policy, and Israel's foreign ministry said it will demand an explanation.
local.title: Prominent Israeli settler denied entry into France

local.h: French schools hit by hoax bomb threats
local.b: Macron said it was too early to say whether a foreign power was behind the threats, which also reached schools in the UK and Ireland.
local.title: France reports school hoax bomb threats

local.h: EES glitches leave travellers wrongly accused of overstays
local.b: Several British travellers say the EU's new biometric border system miscounted their 90-day Schengen allowance, leaving some facing travel bans or large fines.
local.title: Travellers accused of overstaying EU's 90-day rule after being caught in EES chaos

local.h: France to add 70 'medical buses' for rural areas
local.b: The government will deploy 70 more mobile clinics by 2027, bringing the total to 100, to bring GPs and specialists to medical deserts.
local.title: 70 new 'medical buses' to be deployed in rural France

local.h: Russia bans two French lawmakers and two journalists
local.b: Moscow barred four French citizens in retaliation for France's July expulsion of former RT France head Xenia Fedorova, whom Paris called an agent of influence.

local.h: Zemmour enters French presidential race
local.b: Far-right Reconquete leader Eric Zemmour declared his candidacy, pledging two million fewer immigrants by the end of a five-year term. Marine Le Pen remains widely projected to lead the first round.

local.h: O'Donnell claims win in WA Supreme Court race
local.b: King County Superior Court Judge Sean O'Donnell leads appeals court Judge Ian Birk by 39,000 votes in the state's closest Supreme Court race.
local.title: O’Donnell declares victory in tight WA Supreme Court race

local.h: Seattle-area PE teachers shrug off revived fitness test
local.b: Schools have largely ignored the new federal fitness test, which isn't mandatory, and many PE teachers say testing makes kids associate exercise with public shame.

local.h: Washington schools chief Reykdal won't seek reelection
local.b: Superintendent of Public Instruction Chris Reykdal, in his third term, cited his belief in term limits but hasn't ruled out another public role.
